competitors.name: mean_reversion
competitors.rules: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.

competitors.name: You
competitors.rules: Your real Robinhood account, rebased to the shared origin so it's comparable. Performance only — holdings and trades are deliberately not published.

competitors.name: congress_mirror
competitors.rules: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

regime.note: The Federal Reserve lists an October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Low confidence and 70% cash reflect policy risk, near-term binary company events, expensive screen leaders, and the analyst book's persistent negative alpha.

analyst.thesis: Trim, but do not abandon, the September 29 event-driven reset through the October 13 settled session. VRTX and NEM still have falsifiable company-confirmed catalysts: Newmont reports Q3 after the October 22 close, Vertex reports Q3 after the November 2 close, and Vertex has a November 30 povetacicept PDUFA date. However, VRTX fell 4.30% on October 13 and NEM fell 1.33% while SPY fell only 0.01%. The persisted analyst book is down 15.8% versus SPY up 3.7%, or -19.5 points of alpha, with a -3.37 annualized Sharpe. The full-universe screen is also crowded: MRNA gained 50.41% over 20 sessions and 263.51% over 60; SHOP, PLTR, and several software leaders trade at premium or negative earnings multiples. Robinhood data shows VRTX at 28.229339x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.595987x. Reduce VRTX to 16%, NEM to 14%, and hold 70% cash. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve lists a two-day FOMC meeting for October 27-28, 2026, with a press conference on October 28.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept in IgAN.
Vertex says it will report Q3 2026 results on November 2 after market close and host its call at 4:30 p.m. ET.
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood's October 14 data shows VRTX at 28.229339x P/E, $125.2512 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9259 mean analyst target.
Robinhood's October 14 data shows NEM at 14.595987x P/E, $118.6874 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target.
At the October 13 settled close, VRTX was $485.22, NEM was $115.59, and SPY was $778.01; VRTX fell 4.30%, NEM fell 1.33%, and SPY fell 0.01% from October 12.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
Vertex's sharp October 13 decline may reflect information not captured by the scheduled-catalyst framework.
NEM is below the paper entry; gold-price reversal, cost inflation, or weak Q3 production can overwhelm the valuation case.
A 70% cash balance creates substantial opportunity cost if risk assets continue higher.
The persisted portfolio alpha is -19.5 points with a -3.37 annualized Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept, and Vertex confirmed Q3 results for November 2. The October 13 close was $485.22; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 28.229339/6.071210, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9259 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Approval can establish a nephrology franchise faster than the market credits, but the 4.30% one-day decline, binary outcome, and negative portfolio alpha require trimming the anchor from 20% to 16%. [DATA] Buy limit $490.07, about 1% above the settled close.
rationale.NEM: [DATA] Newmont confirmed Q3 results after the October 22 close; Robinhood's earnings calendar shows a $1.93 EPS estimate. The October 13 close was $115.59; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 14.595987/3.473310, Q2 revenue of $6.118 billion, Q2 net income of $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Stable production and costs could produce a favorable result versus the $1.93 consensus, but the decline below paper entry and commodity risk require trimming from 16% to 14%. [DATA] Buy limit $116.75, about 1% above the settled close.

reflection.looking_back: Before the October 13 tick, the persisted book was down 15.8% versus SPY up 3.7%, or -19.5 points of all-time alpha, with a -3.37 annualized 42-session Sharpe. On October 13, VRTX fell 4.30%, NEM fell 1.33%, and SPY fell 0.01%; at prior target weights the two positions reduced marked equity by about 1.07%, underperforming SPY by about 1.06 points.
worked: The 64% cash buffer materially reduced the October 13 damage relative to a fully invested two-name book.
VRTX and NEM retain company-confirmed, dated catalysts, so both theses remain falsifiable rather than momentum extrapolations.
missed: Both holdings materially underperformed SPY on October 13, led by VRTX's 4.30% decline.
The prior allocation was still too large for a book with -19.5 points of all-time alpha and a -3.37 Sharpe.
reflection.adjustment: Cut VRTX from 20% to 16%, cut NEM from 16% to 14%, lower confidence from 0.31 to 0.29, and raise cash from 64% to 70% until the October and November catalysts validate the positions.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 141 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-10-13, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
